title: Map layer controls: roads and RRC
closeType: HONEST PARTIAL — three of four work items shipped; the fourth is a proposal awaiting an operator ruling, by instruction
missionPremise: Operator request, 2026-08-19, verbatim: 'in the map tools i need a way to turn our road nodes on and off and they should probably be defaulted to off for now' and 'all the RRC data should be able to toggle on and off as well (this is going to take some thinking through because there are many layers to it)'. Ruled into the plan of record as P-46 under OPS-16 amendment A-019 (VERIFIED at source, OPS-16 line 116). The dispatch adds a binding constraint of its own: rrc-wells has a reachable ceiling of one county because its source is Harris-only, so any control implying statewide RRC well coverage asserts something false.
completionPredicate: A stranger opens the LAYERS panel on Property Explorer and on Command Center and can (a) turn the Hauska road-node overlay off and on, finding it OFF on a cold open, and (b) read, without asking anyone, which layers will draw nothing and why. The RRC grouping is REPORTED, not shipped, until the operator has seen it.
scopeBasis: The dispatch named packages/map-renderer/src/chrome/LayersControl.tsx and the layer registry as owned, and apps/command-center/** as lane SS-W8's. apps/property-explorer/** was neither granted nor forbidden, and the road-node street band is rendered THERE with a hardcoded visible:true — so a road toggle that does not touch PE cannot exist. PE edits were therefore taken as in scope, declared in CP1 BEFORE building rather than rationalized after, and held to the minimum that wires the registry key through. Deliberate exclusions: no RRC restructuring (instructed), no deploy (instructed), no merge (instructed), no change to the other five inert layers beyond giving them a basis, no touch of the county-ledger rails themselves.

workItems.title: Road nodes toggle, defaulted OFF
workItems.whatWasActuallyWrong: There was no toggle to default off. apps/property-explorer/src/browse/road-overlay.ts set `visible: true` as a LITERAL on the street ROW band spec, with no visibility parameter reaching it. Only the pedestrian child was switchable. The briefing implied a default flip; it was an ADD.
workItems.howItWasDone: New registry key `road-nodes` (label 'Road nodes (ROW)', group parcel, live:true, CONTEXT role). New `streetVisible` flag on RoadOverlayVisibility that DEFAULTS FALSE, so a caller who forgets to thread the toggle gets the operator's requested default rather than the old always-on behaviour. ExplorerMap threads visibleLayers.has('road-nodes'), with a `: false` pre-seed fallback so the band does not flash on for the first frames. PE's COLD_OPEN_OFF_BY_DEFAULT carries the key; CC already cold-opens parcel-only.
workItems.invariantPreserved: Render filter is not data filter. The near-bbox fetch is untouched, and the band spec still ships its geometry when hidden — a hidden layer and an absent layer stay different states, pinned by a test.

workItems.title: RRC layer controls
workItems.status: PROPOSED, NOT BUILT — by instruction ('do not ship a structure the operator has not seen')
workItems.recommendation: Option C: one parent row 'Texas RRC (oil & gas)' over indented 'Wells' and 'Pipelines' children. Parent is a bulk on/off and carries NO coverage language; every coverage statement sits on a child where the denominator is real. Fallback is option B, two flat rows. Rejected option A, the status quo single toggle, because it is the thing that asserts something false.
conditionsAttached: C2 each child carries its ceiling, its denominator and the ceiling's timestamp; unknown is written as unknown and never as 254
C3 both children ship as honest-empty rows because neither has a map data path today
C4 texas-rrc is re-pointed as the parent id, not deleted, so its paint, stack slot and role survive
workItems.operatorDecisionNeeded: C or B; and whether RRC rows belong on Property Explorer at all or stay Command-Center-only until a data path exists. Lane recommends CC-only.

workItems.title: Score against reach, not against 254
workItems.status: SHIPPED as a mechanism, populated where a ceiling is known
workItems.howItWasDone: Registry rows may declare { ceiling, denominator, basis, asOf }. `ceiling: null` renders as UNKNOWN and is NEVER back-filled with the denominator, because that converts 'nobody probed it' into 'reaches everywhere'. texas-rrc declares unknown and quotes both underlying rails verbatim. A test asserts the rendered string contains 'Reach unknown of 254 counties' and does NOT contain 'Reaches 254 of 254'.

workItems.title: Layers with no data read as honestly empty
workItems.whatWasActuallyWrong: Command Center seeds its LAYERS panel from the WHOLE registry (LiveMapTile.tsx:181-183), so six source-less rows rendered as ordinary checkboxes. Ticking one produced a blank map and no explanation — an empty layer and a broken layer were indistinguishable. This was live before any RRC work and is not RRC-specific.
workItems.howItWasDone: Each affected row declares an `emptyBasis` on the registry, so the reason lives next to the layer it describes rather than as a hardcoded UI string that can drift from it. The shared control renders a 'no data' tag plus the basis line. The checkbox stays OPERABLE — disabling it would hide the layer's existence, and the point is disclosure.

findingsContradictingTheBriefing.briefingSaid: 'The registry today carries rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines and texas-rrc as separate keys with different reach.'
findingsContradictingTheBriefing.sourceSays: Two different registries that do not overlap. The MAP LAYER registry (packages/map-renderer/src/layer-registry.js) carries exactly ONE RRC key, texas-rrc. rrc-wells and rrc-pipelines are COUNTY-LEDGER RAIL keys declared at apps/command-center/src/admin/control/panels/countyManifestTypes.ts lines 142-143, and neither string appears anywhere in packages/map-renderer.
findingsContradictingTheBriefing.whyItMatters: The RRC work is a DECOMPOSITION of one inert map key into subjects that exist only as coverage rails, not a regrouping of three live map layers. That is a larger change than the briefing implies and it is precisely why the grouping question needed an operator ruling rather than a quick refactor.

findingsContradictingTheBriefing.finding: texas-rrc draws nothing anywhere, on either app. It has never had a data path in this repo.
findingsContradictingTheBriefing.whyItMatters: The dispatch warns against a control implying statewide RRC well coverage. The sharper problem is that RRC map coverage is currently zero, so ANY RRC toggle shipped today is a toggle over an empty set. That is why condition C3 makes honest-empty rows a precondition of the grouping rather than a nicety.

findingsContradictingTheBriefing.finding: The blank-checkbox defect is already live on Command Center and is not RRC-specific: six inert rows behave this way because CC seeds `known` from the whole registry while PE filters to live-wired rows.
findingsContradictingTheBriefing.whyItMatters: Work item 4 turned out to be a fix for a shipped defect, not a precaution for a future one.

findingsContradictingTheBriefing.finding: There was no road-node toggle to default OFF. The street band carried `visible: true` as a literal.
findingsContradictingTheBriefing.whyItMatters: Work item 1 was an ADD, not a default flip.

selfCorrection.what: This lane's first honest-empty gate was VACUOUS — it asserted on an accessor that falls back to a generic sentence, so it passed unconditionally. Deliberately stripping a declared basis left the suite at 110 pass / 0 fail: the gate did not notice its own subject being removed.
selfCorrection.howFound: Ran the negative suite before trusting the gate (DEV_PROCESS 2.2). The paired ceiling mutation fired; the silence on this one was legible only by contrast.
selfCorrection.fix: The assertion now reads the declared registry field. Re-applying the same mutation gives 110 pass / 1 fail, exit code 1 read from the command itself rather than through a pipe (DEV_PROCESS 2.3). A second test pins the runtime fallback so both halves are covered.
selfCorrection.note: Same defect class as the special-district writer whose verify could never return non-zero. Recorded here because a lane that hides its own near-miss teaches nobody anything.

road-nodes default OFF — enforced by test rather than by care, because adding a live:true registry row auto-joins PE's known set and the cold-open set is 'everything known except the off-by-default list', so a forgotten entry silently ships the OPPOSITE of the operator's request with no error anywhere.

Checked because a toggle wired to a field the renderer ignores passes every unit test and does nothing on a real map.
